author: high
claim: For every nonnegative integer k, the sum from j=0 to k of 2^(k-j) binom(k+j,j) equals 4^k.
evidence: Fix a nonnegative integer k and consider all binary strings of length 2k+1. For each j in {0,...,k}, count strings in which the (k+1)-st occurrence of 1 is at position k+j+1. In the first k+j positions there must be exactly k ones and j zeros, which can be arranged in binom(k+j,j) ways; the last k-j positions are arbitrary, giving 2^(k-j) choices. These disjoint cases exhaust exactly the strings containing at least k+1 ones, so the displayed sum counts the strings with a strict majority of ones. Since 2k+1 is odd, every binary string has a strict majority of exactly one of the two bits. Bitwise complementation is a bijection from the strict-majority-one strings to the strict-majority-zero strings. Hence the former constitute half of all 2^(2k+1) strings, and their number is 2^(2k)=4^k.
